- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops), model often underestimates the drop — adjust downward bias in forecast midpoints.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 5d), model frequently overshoots in next 3–7 days — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true peak.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 7+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overestimate future prices — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust — delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes or next 30d window.
- For 30d forecasts, model underestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods — increase forecast spread (±1.5–2.0%) to reflect higher uncertainty.
- If sentiment history includes multiple -1.00 entries, model tends to overreact to short-term noise — filter out 1–2 extreme outliers in forecast tail.
